Element 16 measured the test site for potential layout options, documented the existing equipment and foundation on-site, received feedback on potential thermal storage interconnection options, valve material selection, heat transfer fluid reservoir sizing, foundation modifications and obtained further technical details including heat transfer fluid data, piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&ID). Solar Technology Applied Research and Testing (START) Lab: Element 16 was introduced to Kenneth Ritter, the then Director of Cleco Alternative Energy Center at Univ of Louisiana, Lafayette by Glenn Reynolds (Gossamer Space Frames). The START lab includes an operational DOE-funded CSP plant for testing. Element 16 participated in a virtual meeting with Kenneth Ritter to understand the system specifications and explored the possibility of using this facility for prototype testing. The system has a total of 12 large aperture trough (LAT) developed by Gossamer Space Frames and can generate a nominal thermal output of 650 kWt. Although the system used water as the heat transfer fluid to power an organic rankine electric power unit, it was clarified that the trough receiver system was rated for temperatures of 400 oC and one of the blocks could be isolated with minimal modifications and used for testing purposes. For the maximum charge rate of 60 kWt proposed for prototype testing in Year 3, it was determined that only 2 to 3 out of the 12 blocks would be sufficient. Element 16 also determined there was sufficient footprint available in the facility for sulfur TES system installation. Engagement with industrial customers The technoeconomic analysis conducted during budget period 1 and discussed in Task 2.0 showed that solar multiple of 3.0 with TES discharge capacity of 10 to 12 hours provides the least levelized cost of heat for industries located in southwest US. In addition, Element 16 team also interacted with solar thermal providers such as Heliogen and Hyperlight Energy, and Petroleum Development of Oman, the owner and operator of the Miraah solar thermal facility, to receive information of typical design peak heat rate the solar field is designed for. Based on the above discussions, Element 16 finalized the operation process parameters for pilot sulfur thermal storage design as follows: a. Charge Peak Heat Rate – 2x discharge rate (Corresponding to solar multiple of 3.0) b. Charge Temperature – 290 to 305 oC c. Discharge Temperature – 140 to 200 oC (approximately, 6500 TBtu (47%) of US IPH requirement is in this temperature range [1,2]) d. Discharge Time – 10 to 12 hours e.
